summary: Cache Creek-Ashcroft Regional Airport (YZA) is a medium-sized airport serving the twin communities of Cache Creek and Ashcroft in British Columbia's southern interior. Located along the historic Cariboo Wagon Route corridor, the airport supports general aviation, wildfire response operations, and occasional charter flights in this semi-arid ranching region. Its position near Highway 97 makes it a useful gateway for visitors exploring the Gold Country and surrounding grasslands.
faqs:
Q: Where is Cache Creek-Ashcroft Regional Airport located?
A: The airport is situated near the village of Cache Creek in British Columbia, Canada, approximately 10 km south of the town center, serving both Cache Creek and the nearby community of Ashcroft.

Q: Does the airport offer commercial passenger service?
A: No, YZA does not operate scheduled commercial flights. It primarily serves general aviation, private aircraft, charter operations, and emergency services including aerial wildfire suppression.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features a paved runway suitable for medium-sized aircraft, basic tie-down areas, and limited services. Pilots should coordinate any fuel or hangar needs in advance as on-site amenities are minimal.

Q: When is the best time to fly into YZA?
A: Summer and early fall offer the most favorable flying conditions, with long daylight hours and generally stable weather. Winter operations can be affected by snow and valley fog common to the Thompson-Nicola region.
transport_tips: The airport is most easily accessed by car via Highway 97, located just outside Cache Creek with a short drive into town. Rental vehicles are not available on-site, so arranging transportation in advance through local operators in Cache Creek or Kamloops is recommended. The nearest major city with full services, Kamloops, is approximately 90 km north along Highway 97.
local_tip: Before flying in, contact the airport manager to confirm current runway conditions and any temporary closures, especially during fire season when the airport frequently activates as a wildfire response base and airspace can become restricted.
